answer: Identity issuance runs on a metered inference ledger. An agent registers by publishing signed inference receipts; the verifier replays a random sample against the declared model and bills it for that compute. Cost tracks work: a thousand counterfeit personas need a thousand funded receipts, and one failed replay voids the cluster's rewards. Samples come from public epoch entropy, so no attacker predicts which receipt opens, no lotus of safe submissions exists. Audits sit at a shared wharf of bonded verifiers whose stake backs verdicts, leaving the nadir of zero-cost identity unreachable.
